# Who is responsible, and what changed since

*Generated by `alicia/scripts/responsibility_note.py` on 29 October 2026 from the register (DECISIONS E-94). Draft: compiled by AI-assisted desk research from the sources cited; not yet checked by a person.*

Every register item now names the government bodies responsible for it (337 tags on 234 items, from 105 bodies in `regulation-register/bodies.json`), and 29 items record later changes to their law or setting (33 events). 2 items have ended: Sydney CBD and Kings Cross lockout and last-drinks laws (NSW) (repealed 8 March 2021); As-of-right taxi licences at a set annual fee (Victoria) (replaced 2 July 2018).

## Roles

| Role | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Administers | The department whose minister administers the law or runs the program, under the jurisdiction's administrative arrangements; for some state schemes, the agency in the department that runs it |
| Regulates | The body that licenses, enforces, collects or monitors under the law |
| Leads policy | The department that leads policy on an issue that is not a single law (a non-legislative barrier) or on a national scheme |

Agencies and regulators name the department they sit in, so the legislation menu's *Responsible* filter includes a department's agencies when the department is chosen. Each tag cites its source; `alicia validate` checks that every body exists and every item has a body that administers it or leads policy.

## Later changes

Changes that another register item describes link to it (the date and source are that item's commencement); the rest cite official sources. The menu shows them in each item's timeline, and items repealed or replaced are marked as no longer in force.

| Item | Date | Change | What changed | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Weeknight trading to 9pm in metropolitan Perth (WA) | 26 Aug 2012 | Eased | Sunday and public holiday trading allowed in metropolitan Perth. | register: `wa-trading-hours-sunday-2012` |
| Wheat export single desk abolished | 1 Oct 2014 | Eased | The Wheat Export Marketing Act 2008 was repealed after the accreditation scheme and port access test were removed: bulk wheat exports became fully deregulated, with port access left to an industry code and competition law. | [source](https://aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Bills_Legislation/Bills_Search_Results/Result?bId=r4783) |
| Tackling Alcohol-Fuelled Violence: 2am statewide trading cap (Queensland) | 14 Feb 2017 | Eased | A bill was introduced to repeal the 1am lockout, due on 1 February 2017, retrospectively from that date after an evaluation found a lockout unlikely to change assault trends; 3am service with no lockout was allowed in all 15 safe night precincts. | [source](https://documents.parliament.qld.gov.au/tableOffice/BillMaterial/170214/Liquor.pdf) |
| Petroleum Retail Marketing Sites and Franchise Acts repealed; Oilcode introduced | 14 Mar 2017 | Amended | The Oilcode was remade as the Competition and Consumer (Industry Codes—Oil) Regulations 2017 (registered 14 March 2017). | [source](https://www.legislation.gov.au/F2017L00223) |
| Ride-booking legalised (Queensland) | 1 Oct 2017 | Amended | Booked hire licences and booking entity authorisation commenced. | register: `qld-booked-hire-licences-2017` |
| Pharmacy location rules | 21 Feb 2018 | Extended | Sunset on the location rules removed, so they continue indefinitely. | register: `cth-pharmacy-location-rules-2018` |
| As-of-right taxi licences at a set annual fee (Victoria) | 2 Jul 2018 | Replaced | The Commercial Passenger Vehicle Industry Act 2017 came into full operation: taxi licences gave way to registration and accreditation, and ride-share became legal. | register: `vic-rideshare-2017` |
| Retail electricity price deregulation (NSW) | 1 Jul 2019 | Tightened | A Default Market Offer price cap applied to standing offers. | register: `cth-default-market-offer-2019` |
| Retail electricity price deregulation in south-east Queensland | 1 Jul 2019 | Tightened | A Default Market Offer price cap applied to standing offers. | register: `cth-default-market-offer-2019` |
| Retail energy price deregulation (South Australia) | 1 Jul 2019 | Tightened | A Default Market Offer price cap applied to standing offers. | register: `cth-default-market-offer-2019` |
| Retail energy price deregulation (Victoria) | 1 Jul 2019 | Tightened | The Victorian Default Offer re-regulated standing offer prices. | register: `vic-default-offer-2019` |
| Sydney CBD and Kings Cross lockout and last-drinks laws (NSW) | 14 Jan 2020 | Eased | Lockout repealed in the Sydney CBD Entertainment Precinct; Kings Cross kept its lockout. | register: `nsw-lockout-repeal-cbd-2020` |
| Foreign investment screening | 1 Jan 2021 | Tightened | A national security test, a call-in power for unnotified investments and higher penalties took effect under the Foreign Investment Reform (Protecting Australia's National Security) Act 2020. | [source](https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2020A00114) |
| Sydney CBD and Kings Cross lockout and last-drinks laws (NSW) | 8 Mar 2021 | Repealed | Remaining lockout in Kings Cross removed and last drinks moved to 3.30am: the lockout laws ended. | register: `nsw-lockout-repeal-kings-cross-2021` |
| R&D Tax Incentive replaces the R&D tax concession | 1 Jul 2021 | Amended | Offsets redesigned with premium rates and R&D intensity tiers. | register: `cth-rd-tax-incentive-2021` |
| Adelaide CBD tourist precinct trading hours (SA) | 1 Nov 2022 | Eased | Sunday trading from 9am and Boxing Day trading allowed. | register: `sa-trading-hours-2022` |
| Consumer Data Right: open banking | 15 Nov 2022 | Extended | Consumer data sharing extended to the energy sector, starting with the largest retailers. | [source](https://cdr.gov.au/rollout/cdr-energy-sector) |
| Stamp duty on residential property transfers (New South Wales) | 16 Jan 2023 | Amended | First Home Buyer Choice let eligible first-home buyers pay an annual property tax instead of transfer duty. | [source](https://www.revenue.nsw.gov.au/grants-schemes/previous-schemes/first-home-buyer-choice) |
| Planning and zoning restrictions (New South Wales) | 26 Apr 2023 | Eased | Business and industrial zones replaced by broader employment zones. | register: `nsw-employment-zones-2023` |
| Instant asset write-off threshold increases and temporary full expensing | 1 Jul 2023 | Amended | Temporary full expensing ended; the write-off threshold for small businesses (turnover under $10 million) was set at $20,000 for 2023-24 and 2024-25. | [source](https://www.ato.gov.au/about-ato/new-legislation/in-detail/businesses/small-business-support-20000-dollar-instant-asset-write-off) |
| Stamp duty on residential property transfers (New South Wales) | 1 Jul 2023 | Amended | First Home Buyer Choice closed to new buyers; the first-home buyer duty exemption rose to $800,000 and the concession to $1 million. | [source](https://www.revenue.nsw.gov.au/grants-schemes/previous-schemes/first-home-buyer-choice) |
| Unfair contract terms protection extended to small business | 9 Nov 2023 | Tightened | Unfair contract terms made illegal, with penalties, and small business protection widened. | register: `cth-uct-penalties-2023` |
| Planning and zoning restrictions (New South Wales) | 13 May 2024 | Eased | Mid-rise housing permitted near designated railway stations. | register: `nsw-transport-oriented-development-2024` |
| Remaining import tariffs | 1 Jul 2024 | Eased | Several hundred 'nuisance' tariffs abolished under the Customs Tariff Amendment (Incorporation of Proposals and Other Measures) Act 2024. | [source](https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2024A00117) |
| Pharmacy location rules | 1 Jul 2024 | Extended | The Eighth Community Pharmacy Agreement took effect, to 30 June 2029; it refers to the location rules made under s 99L and provides for consultation on them. | [source](https://www.health.gov.au/sites/default/files/2024-06/eighth-community-pharmacy-agreement.pdf) |
| Insurance duty (Victoria) | 1 Jul 2024 | Amended | Duty on business insurance began falling by one percentage point a year, to zero in 2033. | register: `vic-business-insurance-duty-phase-out-2024` |
| Vapes restricted to pharmacy supply | 1 Oct 2024 | Eased | Pharmacists may supply therapeutic vapes (nicotine up to 20 mg/mL) to adults without a prescription, as a pharmacist-only medicine. | [source](https://www.tga.gov.au/products/unapproved-therapeutic-goods/therapeutic-vaping-goods/vaping-hub/vapes-information-pharmacists) |
| Right to disconnect | 26 Aug 2025 | Extended | The right to disconnect began to apply to employees of small businesses (fewer than 15 employees). | [source](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/newsroom/media-releases/2025-media-releases/august-2025/20250826-right-to-disconnect-starts-for-small-business-employees-media-release) |
| Ride-sharing legalised with taxi reform package (SA) | 8 Dec 2025 | Amended | Metropolitan taxi licence cap removed, with buyback payments and annual licences. | register: `sa-taxi-licence-reform-2025` |
| Mandatory fuel price reporting, Servo Saver (Victoria) | 10 Mar 2026 | Tightened | Retailers must commit a day ahead to a maximum price. | register: `vic-fuel-price-commitment-2026` |
| Mandatory fuel price reporting, MyFuel NT (Northern Territory) | 20 Apr 2026 | Amended | Next-day price commitments replaced real-time price reporting. | register: `nt-fuel-price-commitment-2026` |
| Non-compete clauses in employment contracts | 7 Sep 2026 | Announced | Exposure draft of a ban on non-compete clauses for workers below an income threshold released for consultation (see the related reform). | [source](https://consult.treasury.gov.au/c2026-801178) |
| Card surcharges limited to the cost of acceptance | 1 Oct 2026 | Tightened | Surcharges banned on eftpos, Mastercard and Visa payments, with lower interchange caps. | register: `cth-card-surcharge-removal-2026` |

## Open checks

Where a source could not be read directly, a note says so: on the tag, or for Tasmania on the department in `bodies.json`.

| Caveat | Tags |
|---|---|
| NSW: the allocation of the Act was not checked | 20 |
| SA: the body was confirmed through search results | 20 |
| Tasmania: the department was read through a summarising fetch of the order | 17 |
| Other: a detail not checked (named in the note) | 2 |

- The NSW tags place each Act with the agency that runs it and that agency's department; the Allocation of the Administration of Acts should be checked when the NSW legislation site can be read.
- History is recorded where a later change was found; an item with no history may still have been amended. Coverage is fullest for items that other register items change.
